disclaimer: These are safety-override rules. If ANY red flag matches, risk is immediately set to URGENT.

red_flags.name: Chest Pain or Pressure
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Do not wait. Chew an aspirin if not allergic.

red_flags.name: Difficulty Breathing
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112). Sit upright. Stay calm and try to breathe slowly.

red_flags.name: Fainting or Unconsciousness
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112). Place the person in recovery position. Check breathing.

red_flags.name: Seizure or Convulsions
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112). Clear the area around the person. Do NOT put anything in their mouth. Time the seizure.

red_flags.name: Stroke Warning Signs
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112) IMMEDIATELY. Note the time symptoms started. Use FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call.

red_flags.name: Severe or Uncontrolled Bleeding
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112). Apply firm pressure with a clean cloth. Keep the injured area elevated.

red_flags.name: Vomiting or Coughing Blood
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112). Do not eat or drink. Lie on your side.

red_flags.name: Severe Allergic Reaction
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112). If the person has an EpiPen, use it. Lie them down with legs elevated unless breathing is difficult.

red_flags.name: Suicidal Thoughts or Self-Harm
red_flags.action: You are not alone. Call emergency services (112) or a helpline (iCall: 9152987821, Vandrevala Foundation: 1860-2662-345). Stay with someone you trust.

red_flags.name: Very High Fever with Severe Symptoms
red_flags.action: Call emergency services (112). Cool the person with lukewarm water. Do not use ice water.

red_flags.name: Fever in Baby Under 3 Months
red_flags.action: Seek immediate medical care. Fever in babies under 3 months can be serious. Call your pediatrician or go to the emergency room.

red_flags.name: Bleeding During Pregnancy
red_flags.action: Seek immediate medical care. Call your doctor or go to the emergency room. Lie down and rest until help arrives.
